protocol_type: Controller-mastered command-driven low-power mobile memory bus. Commands are encoded on a 7-bit double-data-rate command/address bus (CA[6:0]) referenced to a quarter-speed differential clock CK; each command occupies two CA transfers (rising CK edge then falling CK edge). Data transfers are double-data-rate on DQ, framed by a separately-enabled full-speed Write Clock (WCK) on writes and a DRAM-driven Read Strobe (RDQS) on reads. There is no CKE pin; low-power entry is a CA command bounded by CS.

command_encoding.transfer: Double data rate referenced to quarter-speed CK: each command uses one transfer on the rising CK edge and one on the falling CK edge.

field_legend.WRX: Write X (do not transfer data; fill burst with all-zero or all-one)
field_legend.WXSA / WXSB: Write X select (value to be written for the X-fill)

commands.name: No operation
commands.notes: Idle / wait; does not terminate an in-progress burst.

commands.name: Power-down entry
commands.notes: Enters power-down via the CA bus (PD bit); no CKE pin — lasts until CS next goes high.

commands.name: Read FIFO
commands.notes: Read internal FIFO (training / debug data path).

commands.name: Write FIFO
commands.notes: Write internal FIFO (training / debug data path).

commands.name: Read DQ Calibration
commands.notes: Reads a fixed DQ calibration pattern for read training.

commands.name: Multi-purpose command
commands.notes: Multi-purpose command carrying OP[7:0] operation/mode-register data.

commands.name: Mode register write-2
commands.notes: Second cycle of a mode register write (MA[6:0] address, OP[7:0] data).

commands.name: Self-refresh exit
commands.notes: Exit self-refresh.

commands.name: Self-refresh entry
commands.notes: Enter self-refresh; PD / DSE bits select power-down vs deep-sleep behaviour.

commands.name: Mode register read
commands.notes: Read mode register MA[6:0].

commands.name: Mode register write-1
commands.notes: First cycle of mode register write (MA[6:0] address).

commands.name: Refresh (all-bank / per-bank)
commands.notes: REFab (AB=all banks) or REFpb (per-bank, round-robin); RFM bit selects Refresh Management.

commands.name: Precharge
commands.notes: Precharge bank (BG/BA) or all banks (AB).

commands.name: Write-32
commands.notes: Double-length (BL32) write; column / bank / bank-group addressed.

commands.name: Column Address Select
commands.notes: Carries WCK synchronization (WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR), Write-X select (WXSA/WXSB), and WRX option; primarily prepares the DRAM to synchronize with the imminent WCK clock — it does NOT itself select a column.

commands.name: Masked Write
commands.notes: Write with per-byte data mask (DMI used as data mask).

commands.name: Write
commands.notes: BL16 write; column / bank / bank-group / auto-precharge.

commands.name: Read
commands.notes: BL16 read; column / bank / bank-group / auto-precharge; DRAM drives RDQS.

commands.name: Read-32
commands.notes: Double-length (BL32) read; starting position within the 32-word burst via C0 / B3.

commands.name: Activate-1
commands.notes: First activate cycle (row address high bits, bank / bank group).

commands.name: Activate-2
commands.notes: Second activate cycle (row address low bits); two ACT cycles open a row.

wck_synchronization.WS_FS: Free-Start: starts the WCK clock immediately; may be followed by multiple reads/writes accessing multiple banks.
wck_synchronization.WS_RD: Read-optimized: optimizes WCK timing for an immediately following read command.
wck_synchronization.WS_WR: Write-optimized: optimizes WCK timing for an immediately following write command.
wck_synchronization.rule: The CAS command carries the WS_FS / WS_RD / WS_WR bits to prepare the DRAM to lock its internal WCK phase to CK before the high-speed transfer. Unlike LPDDR4, the CAS command in LPDDR5 comes BEFORE the read or write command and primarily serves this synchronization role (it does not select a column).

channels.name: CK_t, CK_c
channels.description: Quarter-speed differential master clock. Command/address (CA) is sampled at double data rate relative to CK (rising and falling edges). All LPDDR5 command timing is referenced to CK.

channels.name: WCK_t, WCK_c
channels.description: Full-speed differential Write Clock at 4x the CK rate. Enabled only when a transfer is imminent (after WCK2CK sync). Frames write data and pre-synchronizes for reads.

channels.name: RDQS_t, RDQS_c
channels.description: Full-speed differential Read Strobe; DRAM-driven and edge-aligned with read data; enabled only during reads.

channels.name: CS
channels.description: Chip select (active high). First-cycle of a command is identified by CS high. Also bounds the duration of low-power mode (entered via CA command, lasts until CS next goes high) — replaces the CKE pin.

channels.name: CA[6:0]
channels.description: 7-bit double-data-rate command/address bus. A command occupies two CA transfers (rising CK then falling CK).

channels.name: DQ[15:0]
channels.description: Data bus per channel, two x8 byte groups. Double data rate at the WCK / RDQS rate.

channels.name: DMI
channels.description: Data Mask / Data Bus Inversion, per byte group. Carries write data mask for Masked Write, and DBI for power/SI on normal transfers.

channels.name: RESET_n
channels.description: Active-low reset; returns the DRAM to its reset state.

channels.name: ZQ
channels.description: Calibration reference pin; external precision resistor for output-driver / ODT impedance trim.

valid_ready_handshake_rules: There is no per-beat handshake on the wire. Commands are committed on the CA bus referenced to CK; read/write data follows at deterministic latency relative to the WCK / RDQS clock.
Before a high-speed transfer the controller must issue a WCK2CK synchronization (WS_FS / WS_RD / WS_WR via CAS); the DRAM locks its internal WCK phase during this window.
READ data appears on DQ at the defined read latency after the Read command, framed by the DRAM-driven RDQS edge-aligned with DQ.
WRITE data is launched by the controller at the defined write latency, framed by the controller-driven WCK; the DRAM samples DQ on both WCK edges.
tCCD_L / tRRD_L (same bank group) and tCCD_S / tRRD_S (different bank group) govern command spacing in bank-group mode.

frame_format.command_frame: Two CA transfers (rising CK edge + falling CK edge) on the 7-bit CA bus encode one command per the LPDDR5 command encoding table; CS high marks the first cycle.
frame_format.data_frame_BL16: 16-beat burst on DQ framed by WCK (write) or RDQS (read) at full speed (both edges).
frame_format.data_frame_BL32: 32-beat double-length burst on DQ; reads may specify a starting position within the 32-word-aligned burst via the C0 and B3 column bits.
frame_format.row_open_requires_two_ACT: Opening a row requires two commands: Activate-1 (row high bits) then Activate-2 (row low bits), as in LPDDR4.

comparison_to_lpddr4: LPDDR4 column names C0-C9 are renamed in LPDDR5 to B0-B3 and C0-C5; writes must start at a multiple-of-16 address with B0-B3 zero, but reads may request a non-zero value for B3.
LPDDR5 widens the CA bus to 7 bits (from 6 in LPDDR4) and transfers commands at double data rate, so commands arrive at the same time as LPDDR4 despite the quarter-speed CK.
In LPDDR5 the CAS command precedes the read/write and synchronizes the WCK clock (WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR); in LPDDR4 the CAS-2 command followed the column command.
LPDDR5 provides one set of full-speed WCK clocks per byte (vs per 16 bits in LPDDR4).
